Native source-aligned transfer-entropy sensitivity and circular-shift graphics

etr_native_transfer_entropy_visual.Rd

Three independent Python-free native R graphics presenting already estimated discrete transfer-entropy sensitivity, source-only circular-shift null distributions, and conditional transfer entropy. No TE estimator is rerun or adjusted by the plots.

Plotting parameters

result

Native TE parameter sensitivity or circular source-shift test result, including a complete observed statistic and surrogate distribution as relevant.

parameter

One declared TE sensitivity specification parameter.

metric

One native scientific TE sensitivity metric to plot.

filters

Named list fixing other varying parameter dimensions. Ambiguous slices fail rather than silently averaging any cells.

bins

Explicit positive integer histogram bin count or "auto". Explicit bins use equal-width source min/max breaks. The default native R "auto" retains Sturges for backward compatibility. With python_boundary_mode=TRUE, automatic bins use the selected NumPy finite-data estimator and exact bin counts.

python_boundary_mode

Logical. When TRUE with bins="auto", use explicitly declared NumPy-style automatic histogram geometry, without importing or calling Python. Defaults to FALSE.

numpy_auto_policy

Either "relaxed" (the FD/Sqrt/Sturges width rule observed in modern NumPy) or "classic" (classic FD/Sturges fallback observed in older NumPy). Explicit selection is necessary because frozen Python 1.2 declares numpy>=1.26, not a single histogram implementation.

...

Additional base R graphics arguments.

Value

Plots render on the active native R graphics device and invisibly return exact numeric source coordinates or surrogate/observed statistics and histogram count/bin geometry. These are not Matplotlib Axes and therefore are not equivalent public Python return types.

Details

The circular-source-shift null is a statistical procedure under an explicit source wrap-around assumption and is not a causal identification design. In conditional TE the target and conditioning processes remain fixed while the source is shifted. The selected TE multiverse slice is descriptive; no automatic parameter selection or statistical multiplicity correction is inferred. Full public source certification requires typed result-schema equivalence, full NumPy-version-dependent histogram behavior, Matplotlib Axes return identity, and independent review. Finite numerical histogram geometry and bin counts now have explicit source-boundary options, but source-side plotting remains a different graphics backend.
